messages:
alex: quick Q — I have a trace id but I'm not seeing the full request logs in Console. what's the fastest way to get raw log lines for a request_id?

mira: two quick options: Console and CLI. Console is easiest for ad-hoc, CLI is better if you want a permalink or to pipe into tools.

mira: Console path: Observability -> Traces, search the trace id, open the root span, click "Linked logs" (if available). If that doesn't show anything, copy the request_id from span tags and go to Logs -> Search and run: request_id:"<your-id>" OR trace_id:"<your-trace-id>". Set time window +/- 2m from span time.

sam: note: some services only attach request_id at the ingress layer. If you don't see matches, try searching by http.request_id or x-request-id and widen to 10m. sampling may also drop traces but the logs still exist.

mira: CLI example (redwoodctl):
```
# find logs for a request id in the last 15m
redwoodctl logs query --filter 'request_id="abc-123"' --from '15m' --format raw
# OR correlate by trace id
redwoodctl traces get --id def-456 --show-linked-logs
```

mira: if you prefer raw system-level grep (only for on-prem/debug):
```
# tail recent rotated files and look for the id
rg 'request_id="abc-123"' /var/log/redwood/* | sed -n '1,200p'
```

alex: awesome — one followup: any dashboard link I can drop in a ticket?

mira: yep, use the trace permalink (Share -> Copy link in Traces). For logs use the Logs search permalink (after running the query click Share). Quick tip: add ?from= and ?to= params around the span timestamp so the link opens to the correct window.

ops-bot: REMINDER: retention policy for logs is 30 days for prod by default. If this is older, file a support ticket for archival retrieval. :warning:

alex: thanks all, that should do it :+1:
